# sync-engine

> sync-engine is an ESM-only TypeScript library for composing independently implemented stateful behaviors. Concepts own state and behavior; reactions, views, formers, and endpoints connect them at the application level.

This index is for human and software agents that use sync-engine to design,
build, call, or operate an application. It does not describe changes to the
sync-engine repository.

The current release is beta, and only the newest beta is supported. Pin an exact package version and read the [support policy](../../SUPPORT.md) before upgrading or deploying it.

## Installed-package boundary

When this file is under an installed `@mit-sdg/sync-engine` package, use its
package-local links. They describe the installed version; documentation from the
repository's `main` branch may describe a different beta.

Treat `README.md`, `SUPPORT.md`, `docs/user/`, the shipped examples, and the
package's declared public entrypoints as the consumer surface. Do not inspect or
infer contracts from `dist/engine/`, `dist/command/`, other emitted implementation
files, repository source, or deep imports. Those files can change without a
supported API change. If the public documentation and exported TypeScript
signatures do not answer a question, report the public-contract gap instead of
inferring an answer from implementation source.

## Working rules

- Use only the package subpaths listed in the Public API. The package root and deep imports are unsupported.
- Keep concept implementations independent of peer concepts and application composition.
- Keep concept specifications, registered composition documents, complete static instance/type declarations, executable declarations, and generated read-back distinct.
- For new applications, author `design/concepts/*.md`, `design/compositions/*.md`, and `design/types.md`; conventionally pair one composition document with one source module.
- Form-check draft concepts, compositions, concrete types, instances, and bindings with config-free `sync-engine check-design`; then treat the generated config as the implemented design root: use explicit local URLs, exact typed links, and config-based `sync-engine check` for exact assembled-variant resolution and coverage. Do not use the removed vocabulary-module mode. The authored inventory excludes core-owned `RequestBoundary`.
- Author Concept State in SSF. Version 1 retains full text and bounded structural IR; `check-design` parses declarations and owned names, while invariant/prose meaning, storage, and implementation semantics remain manual review and test obligations.
- Put every instance's external bindings all inline or all detached. Direct qualified owned-type dependency cycles are valid; external-to-external targets and alias chains are invalid.
- Treat instances as finite static semantic identities, not dynamic tenants or storage allocation. Configure persistent repositories or namespaces explicitly.
- Give every query an indented body explaining its answers, empty or unknown case, and deterministic ordering for `many`.
- Treat generated TypeScript as a caller contract. Add explicit validators for
  runtime values.
- Do not assume transactions across actions, rollback, replay, restart recovery, distributed serialization, cancellation of accepted work, or exactly-once execution.
- Change application source declarations, regenerate artifacts, and review the
  generated diff.
- Use the reference pages for guarantees. Guides, examples, and generated read-back demonstrate particular constructions.
